subject: spark RStudio error: unsupported URL scheme

messages.author: cb0312e9c60a7720
messages.subject: spark RStudio error: unsupported URL scheme
parts:
Hello,

Your environment: http://spark.rstudio.com:8787/
seems to be not able to download some source data from url.

to reproduce:

require(data.table)
url <- 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheet/ccc?key=ABC&usp=sharing' #link here some of your google spreadsheet
url <- paste0(url,'&output=csv')
all_dt <- fread(url)
all_dt <- read.csv(url)

both, fread and read.csv returns error: unsupported URL scheme
while on RStudio desktop it is working fine.

Regards
Jan

messages.author: 9711d30301c32133
messages.subject: Re: spark RStudio error: unsupported URL scheme
parts:
Hi Jan,

HTTPS downloads in R are notoriously finicky. Does the Google API (and the confidentiality of your data) allow downloading via HTTP? If so, do you have any more luck with that?

If not, there may be some conflict between what we're supporting and Google's SSL Certs that would need to be investigated.

Jeff

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: spark RStudio error: unsupported URL scheme
parts:
To add on to what Jeff said: https downloads are tricky in R (with R's
built-in download.file function), and they are handled by separate
code paths on Mac, Windows, and Linux, so that may explain why it's
different from your desktop RStudio. For example, an https download of
the Google homepage fails on Spark:
> download.file('https://google.com/', 'test.html')
Error in download.file("https://google.com/", "test.html") :
unsupported URL scheme


The downloader package tries to work around these differences on the
different platforms, to make it possible to consistently to use https.
To use it:

install.packages('downloader')
library(downloader)
download('https://google.com/', 'test.html')

-Winston
